processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Spherical Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder (particle diameter 15–53 μm) was PREP-prepared (Advanced Corporation for Materials and Equipments, PREP-22) and used as SLM feedstock; measured composition (wt%, ICP-OES): Mn 29.95, Al 8.63, C 1.20, Ni 3.45, O 0.01, Fe Bal.

processing_steps.method: selective laser melting (SLM) at laser power 130 W
processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (99.99% pure); oxygen content in forming chamber maintained below 300 ppm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Laser power 130 W corresponds to laser energy density 108.33 J/mm³; spot diameter 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.02 mm, hatch space 0.08 mm, scanning speed 750 mm/s; a 67° rotation angle was applied to each layer; samples (75×12×12 mm and 10×10×10 mm) printed on an SLM Solutions SLM280 printer; laser-scanning strategy involved overlapping strips.

structures.overall_structure: SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy mainly comprises the austenite (γ-Fe(M)) phase without any α-Fe(M) phase; the transverse cross-section reveals fine equiaxed grains with random orientations.

phases_present.morphology: fine equiaxed grains with random orientations (different colors in IPF)
nano-sized particles uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix (reported for the SLM-printed alloy)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Right-skewed distribution with modal bar near the 12% level, broader tail with bars up to ~38 μm and a secondary peak around 16–18 μm.
grain_structure.texture: Random orientations, no dominant hue (equiaxed grains)

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile sample with a gauge length of 25 mm and a diameter of 5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Sun's universal testing machine; Reliant electronic extensometer

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Green curve for P-130 in Fig. 12, steep elastic rise followed by a long nearly flat plastic plateau above 1000 MPa ending in a sharp vertical fracture drop.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness tester at a load of 0.5 kg for 10 s; each value is the arithmetic mean of five measurement points
Measured with a laser confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 900)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 Advance X-ray diffractometer, Cu target, continuous scanning, 2°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase constitution of the SLM-printed samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 contains only γ-Fe(M) austenite reflections (no α-Fe(M)); FWHM of the (111) peak = 0.255.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) / inverse pole figures
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Oxford Symmetry S2 EBSD detector; data analyzed with TSL OIM software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: step size 0.3–0.7 μm, accelerator voltage 15–20 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize grain morphology and orientation in the cross-section
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 (Fig. 7(d)) shows coarse equiaxed grains with larger magenta/pink and blue grains separated by fine-grained bands, random orientations.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Leica DMi8 M/C/A optical microscope; samples electrolytically polished in perchloric-acid/ethanol solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 (Fig. 6(d)) shows very few small dark defects and one slightly elongated dark feature; porosity 0.28%.

characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate surface quality and defects at different laser powers
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 (Fig. 11(d)) shows a melt-tracked surface with several distinct spherical droplets labelled 'Balling'.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 (Fig. 13(d)) shows a mixed morphology with 'Dimple' and 'Cleavage'; internal defects (pores and cracks) and spheroidization were observed.

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure surface roughness (Sa) of printed samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: P-130 (Fig. 10(d)) exhibited a surface roughness Sa of 4.65 μm.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determine relative density of each sample

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Sun's universal testing machine; Reliant electronic extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, loading rate 1 mm/min; dog-bone specimen gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
load 0.5 kg for 10 s; five points averaged

unmapped_findings: P-130: relative density 99.12% (relative density first increases then decreases with increasing laser power).
P-130: porosity 0.28% (porosity first decreases then increases with increasing laser power).
P-130: surface roughness Sa = 4.65 μm (surface becomes smoother with increasing laser power).
P-130: FWHM of the (111) γ-Fe(M) diffraction peak = 0.255 (FWHM decreases with increasing energy density).
P-130: reduction of area Z = 34.84% (Table 2, in addition to elongation 39.72%).
P-130: tensile fracture surface shows a mixed dimple + cleavage morphology together with internal pores/cracks and spheroidization (Fig. 13(d)).
P-130: 3D surface topography of the sample shows a maximum height label of 36.05 μm (Fig. 10(d)).

The minimum density among the samples prepared with different parameters is 6.78 g/cm³, much lighter than 304 stainless steel (7.93 g/cm³); this value is only reported for the overall sample set, not specifically for P-130.

Each SLM-printed sample (including P-130) contained austenite as the predominant phase with a small amount of nano-sized κ carbide; TEM evidence of κ carbide with a [011]γ∥[011]κ relationship was obtained for P-110 only.
